plan: Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. With rational opponents, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than my value when an opponent’s bid lies between my value and the inflated bid. Underbidding risks losing when I would have earned positive surplus. No prior rounds to learn deviations; assume rational play this single round. Therefore, bid my value: 36. If I have the highest value, I win and pay the second-highest bid; otherwise I lose and pay nothing.

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. It guarantees winning whenever your value is the highest and paying the second-highest bid, which maximizes expected profit. Any bid shading risks losing when winning would have been profitable and does not lower the payment conditional on winning. With value 33 (uniform draws 0–49), bid 33 to capture all positive-surplus opportunities without overpaying. No history effects matter in a single round; ties are random, and truth-telling remains optimal. ]
